title: Multiplication Table
description: Generate multiplication tables from a single row to a full 10x10 grid with formatted output.

steps.title: Single row of a table
steps.description: Write a function that prints one row of a multiplication table — a number multiplied by 1 through 10.
hints: Use a for loop from 1 to 10
Print number * i for each iteration

verification.failureMessage: The row for 5 should show multiples: 5 10 15 20 25 30 35 40 45 50.

steps.title: Print a table for one number
steps.description: Write a `printTable` function that prints the full multiplication table for a given number (1 to 10).
hints: Print the number times 1 through 10, each on a new line
Format each line as 'number x i = result'

verification.failureMessage: Each line should be formatted like '7 x 1 = 7' through '7 x 10 = 70'.

steps.title: Full 1-10 table
steps.description: Use nested loops to print a complete 10x10 multiplication table.
hints: Print each row on its own line

verification.failureMessage: The table should include all products from 1x1 to 10x10.

steps.title: Format with padding
steps.description: Format the table so columns align properly using padding (spaces to make each value the same width).
hints: Use .toString().padStart(3) in JS to make each entry 3 characters wide

codeTemplate.javascript: // Print the table with aligned columns using padding
codeTemplate.typescript: // Print the table with aligned columns using padding
codeTemplate.python: # Print the table with aligned columns using padding

verification.failureMessage: Use string padding to make all columns line up properly.

steps.title: Multiplication table up to N
steps.description: Write a function that takes a number N and generates a multiplication table from 1 to N.
hints: The outer loop goes from 1 to N instead of 10
The inner loop also goes from 1 to N

verification.successMessage: Nested loops create a 5x5 table — no 6s or above!
verification.failureMessage: For N=5, the largest value should be 25 (5x5) and there should be 5 rows.
